opener_concept: A hoodie that was £20 last month costs £25 now. Box 1 asks how many pounds the price went up (pure common sense). Box 2 asks what that £5 is as a percentage of the old £20. The reveal names it as percentage change: find the change, then compare it with what you started from, and warns about comparing against the new value. Two price labels are drawn as a self-contained inline SVG so the figure claimed is actually shown.
notes: All 20 problems are text-data or chart-data, so every answer was fresh-solved; the 5 gold and 11 other stored solutions verified correct as stored. Six displays were edited only to break duplicate answers inside a tier (the validator rejects repeats) or to remove a decimal-place instruction that conflicted with the stored value. Both Chart.js configs (silver[0] employment sectors, gold[2] country populations) preserved byte-for-byte; no images exist in this lesson and none were invented. All 40 catch-all check:'wrong' misconceptions were deleted and rebuilt as expect-matched diagnoses derived by actually committing each error (e.g. remaining-as-percentage-of-original, new-as-percentage-of-original, forgot the ×100, gave the raw difference, read the wrong chart series, added two percentage changes together); several old messages stated the correct answer outright and none now do. Added guided_steps to all 20 problems (no multiple choice in this lesson), each with a locating first box: for the two chart problems the first box orients on the legend or the country labels before any reading; for text problems the first box pins down which figure is the starting value or the whole, which is the actual failure point in percentage change. Completion boundary set at the divide step, so locating and finding the change are pre-worked and the student does the division, the ×100 and the check. Every walk ends with a check step that runs the percentage forwards and lands back on a figure from the question. Added tier_guides, all three {tier}_description lines (geography had none), three teach walks not drawn from the bank (dune height, hidden survey total, reservoir with two sequential changes plus a deliberate demonstration of why −25% then +40% is not +15%), and slimmed the method card to 4 steps and 110 words.
